analysis.title: USA: UMich Sentiment Rises; Inflation Expectations Decline
key_insights: The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rose 3.0pt to 51.0 in the November preliminary report, above the median forecast of 48.0 and GS's 49.5.
The current economic conditions component rose 4.3pt to 51.0 and the consumer expectations component rose 2.1pt to 50.9.
Median 1-year inflation expectations fell 0.4pp to 4.3%, well below the median forecast of 4.6% and the prior 4.7%.
Median 5-10-year inflation expectations fell 0.1pp to 3.4%, below the median forecast of 3.5% and GS's 3.5%.
About 57% of respondents spontaneously mentioned that high prices have eroded their living standards. This is the highest since May and up from 46% in February, just before the Iran conflict.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 3.0pt from the prior 48.0. It beat the median forecast of 48.0 and GS's 49.5, a modest improvement in consumer mood.
The actual print of 51.0 came in above both the Street median and the GS estimate.
Down 0.4pp from 4.7%. It came in well below the median forecast of 4.6%, which eases near-term inflation pressure in the survey.
The actual print of 4.3% came in below this forecast.
Down 0.1pp from 3.5%. It came in below the median forecast and GS's 3.5%, a small easing in longer-run inflation expectations.
The actual print of 3.4% came in 0.1pp below this forecast.

risk_factors: About 57% of consumers say high prices have eroded their living standards, the highest since May, so price-level frustration remains elevated despite the sentiment gain.
geopolitical: The University of Michigan survey cites the Iran conflict as the starting point for the rise in consumers' price complaints. Mentions of eroded living standards were 46% in February, just before the conflict.
